required_concepts: Heart rate is discrete because it represents a count of individual beats (each beat is a distinct event)
optional_concepts: Measurement precision (e.g., 72.5 BPM) does not change the discrete nature of the data
Discrete data consists of distinct, countable values
acceptable_paraphrases: Heart rate is discrete as it counts individual beats
It is discrete because each beat is a separate countable unit
Heart rate measurements are discrete data since they represent counts
critical_errors: Claiming it is continuous because measurements can have decimal precision
misconceptions: Believing heart rate is continuous because it can be measured with decimal precision
Thinking continuous data must always involve physical measurements like temperature or weight
grading_notes: Emphasize that discrete data refers to countable events, not measurement precision. Acceptable answers must clearly connect heart rate to counting individual beats rather than continuous measurement.
